- `struct[OutlineItem]` derives `Clone` and `Debug` and carries `#[non_exhaustive]`. It declares the public fields `selector`, `kind`, `span: Span`, `name_span: Option<Span>`, `header_span`, `trailer_span`, `structural_hash: String` and `attachments: Vec<OutlineAttachment>`. It also has the private `own_hash: Option<String>`, which matches the `/* private fields */` entry.
- `impl[OutlineItem]/fn[new]` has the prescribed signature. It initializes `name_span` to `None` and `attachments` to `Vec::new()`, as the text states.
- `fn[with_name_span]` sets `name_span = Some(span)`.
- `fn[with_own_hash]` stores the digest in the private `own_hash`.
- `fn[with_attachments]` sets `attachments` to the supplied list.

behavioral: The reviewed tests cover each observable obligation of `requirements.sdk.outlines.OutlineItem`.

- **Constructor defaults and preserved fields.** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[outline_constructors_preserve_fields_and_replace_attachments]` builds an item with `OutlineItem::new`. Right after construction it asserts that `name_span` is `None`, `attachments` is empty, and `header_span` and `trailer_span` are `None`. After a clone, it asserts that `selector`, `kind`, `span` and `structural_hash` are unchanged.
- **Builders.** The same test chains `with_header_span`, `with_trailer_span` and `with_name_span`. It asserts the resulting `Some(...)` values for all three.
- **`with_attachments`.** The same test calls `with_attachments` twice, first with a `Comment` and then with an `Annotation`. It asserts that only the second list remains, which shows the call replaces the list. It asserts the kind and span of that attachment.
- **`with_own_hash`.** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[explicit_languages_share_configuration_and_retain_their_scheme]` uses `CustomLanguage::outline`, which calls `with_own_hash` on the root item. The test asserts that `structural_hash()` is `"a hello z"`. It asserts that the fingerprint value is `"a  z"` and the scheme is `custom-v2:own-v1`. This shows the own hash is stored separately from `structural_hash` and is the digest used when it is supplied. The test also asserts that a selected item keeps its own `structural_hash`.
- **Trait implementations.** Clone is exercised by `outline.clone()` followed by field assertions. Debug is exercised by `format!("{outline:?}")`. The requirement gives no Debug format, so a non-empty assertion is enough.
- **Cited requirements.** `Span`, `name_span` and `attachments` are cited as context. The tests apply them to this item through the span and name-span values and the attachment ownership shown above, and I did not reassess their own tests.
- **Struct shape and signatures.** These are structural. `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]` checks the public exports against the appendix.

I found no gaps.

`structural_hash` identifies the item’s outline-relevant contents. A language supplies the digest excluding descendants with `with_own_hash` when it differs from the structural hash.
`attachments` lists the source constructs assigned to this item under

pub fn with_name_span(self, span: Span) -> Self;
pub fn with_header_span(self, span: Span) -> Self;
pub fn with_trailer_span(self, span: Span) -> Self;
pub fn with_own_hash(self, hash: String) -> Self;
pub fn with_attachments(self, attachments: Vec<OutlineAttachment>) -> Self;
`trust_but_verify::outline::Span` locates text by byte offsets from the start
of the original source snapshot, including when a caller selects a nested item.
`start` is inclusive and `end` is exclusive. A valid span satisfies
`start <= end <= source.len()` and both offsets are UTF-8 character boundaries.
For `source: &str`, `&source[span]` yields the same slice as
`&source[span.start..span.end]`, with the same bounds and boundary checks.
pub fn new(start: usize, end: usize) -> Self;
A named item's `name_span` is `Some` with the span to highlight for its name
in the original source snapshot. The highlighted text may differ from the
name in the selector. Use `selector` to address the item. The file root and
anonymous items have `name_span` set to `None`. `OutlineItem::new` starts with
`None`. Language providers use `with_name_span` to set the highlight within
to one owning item, which may be the file root. Each item lists the
An *attachment* is a source construct that an outline language associates
with an outline item. A documentation comment on a Rust function and a
decorator on a Python method are examples.
